title: Junta Jet Drops Bomb Near Paletwa Town Entrance, Injuring Two Girls
detail: At around 7:32am on August 11, 2026, a junta fighter jet dropped a bomb near the entrance sign of Paletwa Town, southern Chin State, on the upper Kaladan River. Shrapnel struck the legs of two teenage girls, 19-year-old Ma Htwe Sein and 13-year-old Ma Thandar Hteik, who were in a nearby home. The strike is part of the junta's escalating aerial campaign across AA/CNF-contested townships along the Rakhine-Chin border.

media.caption: Junta jet drops a bomb near the entrance of Paletwa Town, injuring two teenage girls with shrapnel.

title: UN Investigators (IIMM) Say Myanmar Military Has Escalated Airstrikes on Civilians
detail: The UN's Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar (IIMM) reported on August 11, 2026 that the Myanmar military has escalated aerial attacks on civilians, increasingly using low-cost motorized paragliders, gyrocopters, and drones to drop unguided explosives at low altitude — in the upper Sagaing region, some pilots reportedly cut their engines on approach to deny civilians warning. Investigators documented a pattern of 'double-tap' strikes hitting first responders and those aiding the wounded, alongside arbitrary detention, torture, and sexual violence, drawing on evidence from more than 1,600 sources. The IIMM said over 8,000 civilians have been killed and more than 31,000 arrested since the 2021 coup. Separately, the Arakan Army said about 20 civilians were killed and 22 injured in airstrikes across three Rakhine townships from August 1-11, including one raid involving up to eight aircraft over roughly an hour.

media.caption: UN investigators document escalating Myanmar military airstrikes on civilians, including 'double-tap' attacks and low-cost aircraft.

title: KIA-KPDF Intercept Junta Offensive Near Momeik, Northern Shan State
detail: Beginning August 10-11, 2026, roughly 150 SAC troops attempted to advance from junta-held downtown Momeik toward Kachin Independence Army (KIA)-controlled Mabein Township, pushing into territory held by KIA Battalion 34 (Brigade 4) near Upper and Lower Nyaungni villages. Joint KIA and Kachin People's Defence Force (KPDF) units intercepted the column, killing at least one junta soldier and pinning down troops from Light Infantry Battalion 348, including a captain. The junta responded by deploying Mi-35 attack helicopters and a Y-12 transport aircraft to fly heavy airstrikes in support of its stalled column, which also targeted flood-affected areas nearby.

media.caption: KIA-KPDF forces intercept a junta column advancing toward Momeik, prompting heavy junta air support.
